channel.title: The Bias — Latest news
channel.description: One story. Many angles. Original news, with the context to think for yourself.

item.title: DOJ seeks conditional block on Alaska certification
item.description: The Justice Department seeks a conditional Alaska Senate certification block, alleging voter confusion; challengers dispute its authority.

item.title: New York Council Backs Horse-Carriage Ban
item.description: New York's council approved a carriage phaseout by 2028, drawing a promised court challenge from the drivers' union.

item.title: WFP cuts food aid to 700,000 Palestinians
item.description: WFP has reduced food assistance for 700,000 Palestinians across Gaza and the West Bank, citing funding shortages.

item.title: U.S. Orders Non-Emergency Staff Out of Saudi Arabia
item.description: Washington ordered non-emergency staff and eligible family members out of Saudi Arabia, citing Houthi attacks on airports and infrastructure.

item.title: iPhone Duo launch brings sellouts and waits
item.description: Apple’s first foldable reached stores with sellouts, as limited supply left some buyers facing months-long waits.

item.title: Meta’s New Shares Preserve Zuckerberg’s Voting Control
item.description: Meta approved non-voting shares as Zuckerberg pledged eight years of residency in California or wherever it is headquartered, conditional on continued full-time leadership and an unforeseen-circumstances exception.

item.title: Meta Ordered to Pay $25 Billion
item.description: Meta was ordered to pay $25 billion over misleading privacy statements, with an appeal expected.

item.title: Russia frees American teacher Stephen Hubbard
item.description: Russia freed American teacher Stephen Hubbard after more than four years; Trump’s claim of a cost-free release drew challenges.

item.title: PHP security flaws trigger widespread precautionary shutdowns
item.description: Public bodies and private services take systems offline over PHP flaws, amid patching warnings and exploitation reports.

item.title: Oman’s Sultan welcomed for UK state visit
item.description: Britain welcomes Oman’s Sultan for a state visit, with investment and maritime-security agreements expected amid regional conflict.

item.title: SpaceX and Tesla Explore a Possible Merger
item.description: Musk says independent committees are exploring a merger, but no transaction terms have been agreed.

item.title: Musk Pledges SpaceX Shares for U.S. Children
item.description: Musk promises children SpaceX shares through Trump Accounts, but eligibility rules and sale restrictions shape the proposed gift.

item.title: Wainwright Fire Kills Four Canadian Service Members
item.description: Four service members died at CFB Wainwright; 39 injured people remained in hospital as officials investigated the fire.

item.title: Trump waives new Russia sanctions and tariffs
item.description: Trump waives new Russia sanctions and tariffs as critics warn the relief could support Moscow's war effort.

item.title: Most Norte Fire Evacuation Orders Remain
item.description: Most Norte Fire evacuation orders remained Saturday after the blaze damaged or destroyed at least six homes.

item.title: Prosecutor: ICE collision witness sent to Mexico
item.description: A witness was sent to Mexico hours after questioning in the ICE collision inquiry, Houston's prosecutor says.

item.title: Suspicious mail targets election offices and lawmakers
item.description: Federal investigators examine nationwide mailings as preliminary tests find no hazardous material and offices face evacuations.

item.title: Hormuz attacks sink ships and disrupt trade
item.description: GFS Pride sank after a Hormuz attack as escalating strikes reduced oil shipments and widened risks for commercial shipping.

item.title: Justice Department sues California over voter citizenship
item.description: The Justice Department seeks to withhold flagged California mail ballots pending citizenship checks; state officials challenge its evidence.

item.title: Russian Strikes Leave Ukrainians Without Power
item.description: Russian attacks leave at least 600,000 without electricity as Kyiv disputes ceasefire claims and questions allied warnings.

item.title: Ukraine reports strikes after Trump’s energy ceasefire declaration
item.description: Ukraine reported fresh energy strikes after Trump announced a ceasefire that Moscow did not confirm.

item.title: Federal Agents Search Ilhan Omar’s Home
item.description: Federal agents searched Omar’s home weeks before the midterms; she accused the Trump administration of political targeting.

item.title: Trump's Russian Diesel Deal Draws Allied Opposition
item.description: Trump's Russian diesel agreement drew allied and congressional opposition as he called for Ukraine to replace Zelensky.

item.title: Riyadh Airport Attack Kills 12, Halts Flights
item.description: Saudi authorities report 12 deaths at Riyadh airport; Trump says the US may join action against the Houthis.

item.title: Pillay Wins Nobel as US Sanctions ICC
item.description: US sanctions on the ICC followed Pillay's Nobel win, which drew praise and Israeli criticism.

item.title: Israel marks October 7 anniversary amid divisions
item.description: Israel marked October 7's third anniversary with hostages returned, ongoing Gaza strikes and demands for accountability.

item.title: Army Schedules Hasan’s Firing-Squad Execution
item.description: The Army set Hasan’s firing-squad execution for Dec. 3; a civilian court challenge could delay it.

item.title: Trump’s Iran Remarks Prompt California Threat Monitoring
item.description: Newsom ordered threat monitoring after Trump named California cities; the White House and fact-checkers disputed critics’ interpretation.

item.title: Halzen wins physics Nobel for IceCube research
item.description: Francis Halzen wins the 2026 physics Nobel for IceCube and its discoveries of high-energy cosmic neutrinos.

item.title: Supreme Court weighs Boulder climate lawsuit
item.description: The justices heard competing arguments over whether federal law bars Boulder’s climate-damages claims against oil companies.

item.title: G7 Agrees Emergency Oil and Diesel Release
item.description: G7 leaders agreed to release up to 100 million barrels of reserves; Trump ruled out a diesel export ban.

item.title: Justice Department Won’t Reopen Powell Renovation Probe
item.description: The Justice Department says it won’t reopen its Powell investigation, while a new audit could trigger further action.

item.title: Grenfell files reach prosecutors after nine-year investigation
item.description: Grenfell files reach prosecutors, with charging decisions promised before the fire’s tenth anniversary in June 2027.

item.title: Smith Defends Trump Cases Before Senate
item.description: Jack Smith defended his Trump prosecutions as Republicans challenged his methods and accused him of misleading Congress.

item.title: Supreme Court Allows Third-Country Deportations to Resume
item.description: The Supreme Court allowed removals to resume while leaving the policy’s legality unresolved ahead of December arguments.

item.title: Government-Funded Trump Ads Face Propaganda Complaints
item.description: Government-funded Trump ads have prompted oversight complaints and Republican objections; the White House calls them public service announcements.

item.title: Anthropic’s Reported Prospectus Warns of Existential Risks
item.description: Anthropic’s reported IPO prospectus warns of catastrophic AI risks alongside steep losses and vast infrastructure commitments.

item.title: Prosecutors Reopen Inquiry Into Alleged Cornell Rape
item.description: Prosecutors reopened an alleged Cornell fraternity rape investigation after a civil lawsuit, amid disputes over the earlier response.

item.title: Avanti nationalisation set for March 2027
item.description: Avanti will transfer to public ownership in March 2027, with infrastructure investment planned to improve reliability.

item.title: Healey Pledges Tighter Spending Control
item.category: UK fiscal policy and economic growth
item.description: John Healey’s first major speech as chancellor paired a pledge to control public spending with regional investment, deregulation and UK procurement plans, drawing criticism from opposition parties, business voices and the Green Party.

item.title: Trump Rejects Iran’s Hormuz Reopening Proposal
item.description: Donald Trump rejected Iran’s offer to reopen the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for lifting a US naval blockade, removing oil sanctions and restoring a regional ceasefire. Iran says it remains willing to negotiate through mediators, while US officials and allied voices argue that Tehran’s conditions are unacceptable. The dispute has left energy markets strained, exposed sharply different views on sanctions and military pressure, and kept Qatar-led indirect diplomacy alive but uncertain.

item.title: Manchester City Found Guilty of Financial Rule Breaches
item.description: Reports said an independent panel had upheld 114 of 115 Premier League financial-rule charges against Manchester City, although The Guardian described most of 134 charges as upheld and the Premier League had not publicly announced a decision. City says the confidential process remains incomplete and it is confident of proving innocence. The reported case could lead to an appeal, sanctions hearing, compensation claims and a wider argument over competitive fairness, financial regulation and the legitimacy of past results.

item.title: US Envoys Visit Kyiv for Peace Talks
item.description: Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner traveled to Kyiv after meeting Vladimir Putin in Moscow, opening a U.S.-led effort to sustain negotiations involving Ukraine and European partners. The talks produced plans for follow-up but no announced settlement, with territorial demands, security guarantees, winter support and continued fighting still dividing the sides.

item.title: US and Iran Resume Military Strikes
item.category: US-Iran conflict and Strait of Hormuz security
item.description: A renewed US-Iran military exchange has brought regional missile retaliation, disputed civilian-casualty and maritime claims, shipping insecurity, competing diplomatic strategies and forecasts of significant economic consequences for UK households.

item.title: Burnham’s First PMQs With Badenoch
item.description: Andy Burnham’s first Prime Minister’s Questions against Kemi Badenoch centred on the October Budget, fiscal credibility, market pressure, welfare, defence, Brexit, public services and the competing economic arguments of the government, opposition and analysts.
